title: A verse alone (Genesis 1:1)
hook: read Bereshit bara Elohim in Hebrew, by yourself

segments.voice: Yesterday, everyday Hebrew: mazal tov, b'ezrat Hashem, l'chaim, and todah, from the root of Judah's name. Your line was todah. Today, one line of Hebrew, and you do the reading.

A single line of Hebrew, black letters, no English underneath. For a long stretch now, this path has handed you pieces: the shapes of letters, their sounds, the roots hiding inside words. Somebody else always did the reading. Today the roles switch. Here is the line the Torah scroll begins with: Bereshit bara Elohim et hashamayim ve'et ha'aretz. In the King James words, "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth." Today you take it apart yourself, word by word, and put it back together.
screen: `ONE LINE, NO ENGLISH.` → `THE ROLES SWITCH.` → `BERESHIT BARA ELOHIM.`

segments.voice: Go slowly. First, bereshit. The opening letter, bet, is a little word glued on the front: in. Then reshit, beginning. Some readers hear rosh inside it, the word for head, as in Rosh Hashanah, the head of the year. Second, bara, created. Its letters are bet, resh, alef. Now look back at bereshit: bet, resh, alef are its first three letters too. The verb is hiding inside the first word before you even reach it. Elohim follows: God. Third, a word English can't translate at all: et. It's spelled alef, tav, the first letter of the alphabet and the last. In Hebrew grammar it simply points ahead to the thing being acted on. But some readers have seen more in it: the whole alphabet, beginning to end, standing at the start of the world. Fourth, the pair at the end. Hashamayim, the heavens; ha is the. Ve'et ha'aretz, and the earth; ve is and, and there's et again, pointing at the earth too. Everything above, everything below. Now put it back together. Bereshit bara Elohim et hashamayim ve'et ha'aretz. You've just read the Torah's opening line in the language it was written in, one word at a time. That's a verse alone: a line short enough to hold in one breath. Bereshit bara.
screen: `BERESHIT: IN THE BEGINNING.` · `BARA HIDES INSIDE BERESHIT.` · `ET: ALEF TO TAV.` · `THE HEAVENS AND THE EARTH.` · then, large: `BERESHIT BARA ELOHIM.`

segments.voice: Say the verse one word per breath, bereshit, then bara, Elohim, et, hashamayim, ve'et ha'aretz, without rushing to the meaning; then say the whole verse once at your own pace, and if you stumble, start again, since there's no audience. If you pray, you can let the verse itself be your words, the way it opens the Torah each year. Otherwise, let the last two words stay with you: the heavens, and the earth you're sitting on.
screen: `ONE WORD, ONE BREATH.` · `THEN THE WHOLE VERSE.` · `THE HEAVENS, AND THE EARTH.`

segments.voice: A verse alone. Genesis one, verse one, read by yourself in Hebrew: bereshit bara Elohim et hashamayim ve'et ha'aretz. In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. Today's word.
Your line: bereshit bara. In the beginning, created: the Torah's first two words, read by you. Tomorrow, the close of the whole year.

howItsDone: Genesis 1:1 opens the Torah and is read aloud in synagogue each year when the reading cycle begins again after Simchat Torah; some Jewish learners practice reading Hebrew on verses like this one, word by word.
